lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Fabiola, this is Luis. Is this an okay time to talk?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hey, yeah, I was waiting for your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Before we start, is there anything on your mind you want to make sure we get to today?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sounds good to me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How have you been feeling since we last talked?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good. Busy, but good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That's great to hear.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: The research is very clear, you have to eat earlier.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can stop eating at 8, I just need tea at night.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've got a plan in mind already.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I have to do something, I don't want the cancer back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Finishing dinner a little earlier, like by 7, makes the 13 hours a lot easier.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, my sugar was better the weeks I ate earlier. I feel guilty when I skip it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You already did the hardest part, which is starting.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday. It's just me and my husband now, so it's easier.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you mind if I tell you what some people do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Black coffee, tea or water are fine during the fast. They don't break it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'd like to be able to keep up with my grandkids.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes. I'll set an alarm on my phone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That's real progress.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I want to get my energy back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would your family say about these changes?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, this week I'll really do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What do you think the next step should be?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday. My doctor said the same thing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How would things be different if you kept this up?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Got it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know, honestly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What did you notice on the days it went well?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it. I wrote it on the calendar.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You can't be eating at 10 at night.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If you don't do this, your health is going to suffer.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let's put you down to finish eating by 7:30 on 4 nights next week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Like a 8.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If the parties gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll eat a bigger lunch so I'm not starving at night.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Tuesday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Perfect.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Fabiola, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: God bless you.

tags.note: Asks about how she has been feeling
Advises a specific dinner time unprompted
Sees benefit to blood sugar; expresses guilt
Commits to specific days; sees support at home
Shares what is allowed during fast
Personal reason: keep up with grandkids; not explored
Affirms her knowledge of her schedule
Yes/no question on realism of plan
Ambivalent but commits to an alarm step
Desire for more energy; not reflected
Reports self-esteem gain and calendar use
Affirms her choice, though undercut nearby
Warns of health harm; pressure, not collaborative
Sets goal unilaterally without asking her input
Asks for backup plan for barriers

flags.reason: Unsolicited claim that research requires eating earlier; argues rather than eliciting her view.
Corrective, judgmental statement about her late eating; undermines rapport.
Warning about health decline used as pressure; MI non-adherent and fear-based.
Grandkids motivation was not explored or reflected; coach moved on to a closed question.
Set a specific goal for her without asking for her input on the target.

score.summary: Coach used several open questions and affirmations, but repeatedly persuaded with research claims, warnings, and a unilateral goal, which tended to override Fabiola's own change talk. Her motivations (cancer recurrence, energy, grandchildren, blood sugar) were only partly reflected, and the last goal was never reviewed.
strengths: Line 14: affirmed starting as the hardest part, recognizing her effort.
Line 16: asked permission before sharing what others do.
Line 43: asked an open question about a backup plan for barriers, which she answered well (line 44).
Line 32: explored what went well, which elicited self-esteem change talk (line 33).
coaching_tips: Line 8 and line 12: replace the research claim and timing advice with an open question, e.g., 'What do you think about eating earlier?'
Line 34 and line 37: drop the judgment and warning; reflect her concern instead, e.g., 'You want to protect your health and your energy.'
Line 19 and line 24: reflect her grandkids and energy motivations as complex reflections to strengthen change talk.
Line 39: offer the goal as a option, e.g., 'Would it help to pick a target together?' before setting it.
Open the next call by reviewing the last goal, and summarize her change talk before closing.
